title: Signed tensor/pullback exchange on flat K-flat representatives
statement: Fix l,E,n,f:X→Y and the finite coefficient conventions of [def-pur-finite-pullback-tensor-construction], with l invertible on both schemes. Let P,Q be unbounded cochain complexes of the normalized finite coefficient module sheaves on Y, both K-flat with flat terms [def-sfb-proetale-tensor-model]. Write M=Q_Y(P), N=Q_Y(Q), F for the finite derived pullback, mu for finitePullbackTensorConstruction and sigma_X,sigma_Y for the signed derived braidings fixed by the full K-flat model [def-pur-finite-pullback-tensor-braiding]. Then F(sigma_Y(M,N)) followed by mu(N,M) equals mu(M,N) followed by sigma_X(FM,FN). No boundedness, constructibility or flatness of the derived objects is assumed beyond the displayed flat K-flat complex representatives. This statement computes the representative case, not the extension to arbitrary derived inputs.

proof.text: Apply proEtaleCanonicalTensorPullback to P,Q and to Q,P. This provides preservation of the flat K-flat class and the two canonical total-tensor normalization squares.

Use the proved proEtaleSignedTensorPullbackTotal on P,Q. It calculates the ordinary comparison on tensor unit sections, extends by the module sheafification adjunction, and uses the native Koszul braiding formula on each total summand. Additivity preserves the integer sign, including negative degrees. This gives the signed chain square before localization.

Apply the derived quotient to the signed chain square. Use proEtaleCanonicalTensorPullback on (P,Q) and (Q,P) and pullbackTensorBraiding_existsUnique on the source and pulled-back complexes. Naturality of the exact pullback factorization gives the remaining side of the cube; cancel the source representative isomorphism and the tensor of the two target factorization isomorphisms. Identify the uniquely chosen finite tensor models with their explicit restrictions, and transport the square along the unit-normalized realization using naturality. The Lean proof performs these cancellations explicitly.
